nodes.title: Parcel Desk knowledge
nodes.body:
# Parcel Desk knowledge

A small **fictional** pickup service. This map records inspected source, intended behavior and questions. It is a worked example, not a production readiness assessment.

## Areas

- **[[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]** explains the state transition and response boundary.
- [[areas/access|Customer access]] explains whose pickup can be changed.

## Where to begin

Follow [[notes/cancellation-boundary|the cancellation boundary]], then [[notes/route-responses|the route response mapping]]. The ownership rule in [[notes/ownership-check|Customer ownership]] runs first.

There is one confirmed source/spec mismatch: [[gaps/packed-cancellation|Packed cancellation]]. [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner cancellation]] is an open product decision. [[gaps/deployment-evidence|Deployment evidence]] is outside this fixture's verification scope.

See [[01-coverage|Coverage]] and [[runs/example-survey|the example survey]] for limits. Open `graph.html` in a browser or `Map.canvas` in Obsidian. A flagged node does not by itself mean a missing feature.

nodes.title: Coverage and evidence limits
nodes.body:
# Coverage and evidence limits

Return to [[00-index|the index]].

## Pickup coverage

In [[areas/pickups|Pickups]], the service, adapter, CAN-1/CAN-3 and all three tests were inspected. Three existing unit tests passed; they omit the packed success case. Real HTTP responses, concurrent writes and persistent state are outside the fixture.

## Access coverage

In [[areas/access|Access]], the owner guard, CAN-2, DEC-1 and denied-action test were inspected. The test verified that another customer's requested pickup is denied without mutation. Authentication, partner identities and deployed authorization are outside the fixture.

The release check ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the fictional project: **PASS, 3 tests**. This does not prove CAN-1 is satisfied. Static inspection finds the packed mismatch recorded in [[gaps/packed-cancellation|the product gap]].

The source fingerprints describe this shipped fixture. There is no reviewed Git checkpoint embedded in the example because it is a subdirectory of the toolkit, not an independent application repository. Copy the fixture into a temporary Git project before trying incremental commit sync.

No real service, logs or customer data were inspected. The example does not imply those systems are missing from an actual product. [[gaps/deployment-evidence|Deployment evidence]] records that boundary.

nodes.title: Customer access
nodes.body:
# Customer access

The adapter accepts a customer identifier supplied by its caller. The service compares it with the pickup owner before inspecting state. This fixture demonstrates a policy check; it does not authenticate a network request.

- [[notes/ownership-check|Ownership rule]] constrains [[areas/pickups|pickup cancellation]].
- [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner cancellation]] is an undecided extension, not an accepted missing feature.
- [[gaps/deployment-evidence|Deployment evidence]] limits conclusions about real identity handling.

Inspected [service](../../../src/pickups.py), [adapter](../../../src/routes.py), [spec](../../../SPEC.md) and [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py). The other-customer unit test passed. External identity and real user sessions are outside the fixture.

nodes.title: Pickup cancellation
nodes.body:
# Pickup cancellation

This area covers the in-memory transition and its adapter response. It depends on [[areas/access|customer access]] before state changes are considered.

- [[notes/cancellation-boundary|Cancellation boundary]]: the service currently accepts only `requested`.
- [[notes/route-responses|Route responses]]: service exceptions become status values.
- [[gaps/packed-cancellation|Packed cancellation]]: the accepted requirement includes a state the implementation rejects.
- [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner cancellation]]: proposed actor variation awaiting a decision.

Evidence: [service](../../../src/pickups.py), [adapter](../../../src/routes.py), [requirements](../../../SPEC.md), [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py). All four files were inspected. Three existing tests passed during the example check. Real transport, persistence and deployment are not modeled; see [[gaps/deployment-evidence|verification limits]].

nodes.title: The example cannot establish deployed behavior
nodes.body:
# The example cannot establish deployed behavior

Areas: [[areas/access|Customer access]] and [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]. **Kind: verification gap; intentionally outside the example.**

The [spec boundary](../../../SPEC.md) and [adapter module](../../../src/routes.py) identify an in-memory fixture without an HTTP server, identity provider or database. This map cannot establish a deployed application's authentication, HTTP responses, persistence or concurrency.

No real deployment checks were run. The next action for an actual project would be to identify its real entrypoint and environment, then test a representative allowed and denied cancellation. For this example, leave the item open as a coverage boundary; do not build infrastructure just to make the graph green.

The [[notes/route-responses|status mapping]] is supported locally. [[notes/ownership-check|The owner check]] is distinct from authentication. [[01-coverage|Coverage]] records what the local tests actually establish.

nodes.title: Packed pickup cancellation contradicts CAN-1
nodes.body:
# Packed pickup cancellation contradicts CAN-1

Area: [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]. **Kind: product gap; specification conflict.**

CAN-1 in [the accepted spec](../../../SPEC.md) permits a customer to cancel their own `packed` pickup before collection. The state guard in [cancel_pickup](../../../src/pickups.py) permits only `requested`. [cancel_request](../../../src/routes.py) maps the resulting `ValueError` to status 409.

This is a concrete mismatch in the inspected path. The existing three [tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) pass while omitting the packed acceptance case. Passing them is not proof of CAN-1 compliance. The shipped worked report uses static evidence; independent release checks are recorded outside this vault in `VALIDATION.md`.

**Priority:** first within this fixture's accepted cancellation scope. **Next action:** keep CAN-1 or explicitly revise it; if retained, add a failing packed-case regression test before changing the allowlist. Acceptance: the owner can cancel both requested and packed pickups; another customer still receives 403; collected pickups still receive 409; rejected calls preserve state.

See [[notes/cancellation-boundary|current behavior]] and [[notes/route-responses|response mapping]]. [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner support]] is a different decision and does not block this correction.

nodes.title: Partner cancellation needs a product decision
nodes.body:
# Partner cancellation needs a product decision

Areas: [[areas/access|Customer access]] and [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]. **Kind: product plan.**

DEC-1 in [the spec](../../../SPEC.md) explicitly leaves partner cancellation undecided and outside accepted scope. The [adapter](../../../src/routes.py) accepts a customer identity; it provides no separate partner contract.

Absence of that contract is not evidence of a missing accepted feature. Decide who may act on whose behalf, which identity evidence is required and which states are allowed before making an implementation task. Those choices gate partner work only.

[[gaps/packed-cancellation|The accepted customer requirement]] can be addressed independently. [[notes/ownership-check|Today's owner guard]] must remain intact until any replacement contract is explicitly accepted. No partner runtime checks were run because this fixture defines no partner behavior.

nodes.title: Only requested pickups are currently cancellable
nodes.body:
# Only requested pickups are currently cancellable

Area: [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]]. Use this note when changing allowed states or explaining a rejected cancellation.

**Implementation:** `cancel_pickup` checks ownership, then requires `pickup.state == "requested"`. Accepted calls set state to `cancelled`. Any other state raises `ValueError` before the mutation. The [service](../../../src/pickups.py) establishes this behavior; it is not inferred from the graph.

**Intent:** CAN-1 in the [spec](../../../SPEC.md) includes both `requested` and `packed` before collection. The difference is tracked by [[gaps/packed-cancellation|the packed cancellation gap]]. This current note describes code, not agreement with the requirement.

The [[notes/ownership-check|ownership guard]] runs first. The [[notes/route-responses|adapter]] converts state rejection to status 409. Existing tests verify requested and collected cases; they do not cover packed success. See [[01-coverage|coverage]] for the executed test command. A focused packed-case assertion remains a proposed regression test.

nodes.title: The owner check runs before the state check
nodes.body:
# The owner check runs before the state check

Areas: [[areas/access|Customer access]] and [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]].

`cancel_pickup` compares `pickup.customer_id` with the supplied customer ID before checking the state. Mismatch raises `PermissionError`; no mutation occurs. The adapter maps this to status 403. See [the service](../../../src/pickups.py) and [the adapter](../../../src/routes.py).

This supports CAN-2 in [the spec](../../../SPEC.md). `test_other_customer_cannot_cancel` in [the tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) checks a requested pickup, the 403 status and unchanged state. The three-test suite passed during this example's verification; the test does not establish a real authentication boundary.

[[notes/cancellation-boundary|State eligibility]] applies only after the owner check. [[gaps/partner-decision|Partner cancellation]] cannot be inferred from this customer-only contract. Deployed identity remains [[gaps/deployment-evidence|unverified]].

nodes.title: Cancellation exceptions become adapter statuses
nodes.body:
# Cancellation exceptions become adapter statuses

Area: [[areas/pickups|Pickup cancellation]].

The in-process `cancel_request` adapter calls `cancel_pickup`. It returns 403 for `PermissionError`, 409 for `ValueError`, and a 200 result containing the updated state on success. See [the adapter](../../../src/routes.py) and [the called service](../../../src/pickups.py).

[[notes/ownership-check|Ownership]] determines forbidden responses; [[notes/cancellation-boundary|state eligibility]] determines conflicts. The packed scenario reaches the latter guard, which explains [[gaps/packed-cancellation|the requirement mismatch]].

The [existing tests](../../../tests/test_pickups.py) exercise these three response branches with requested, other-customer and collected fixtures; the suite passed. These are dictionary status values, not observed network responses. Real HTTP mapping and authentication are [[gaps/deployment-evidence|outside the example]].

nodes.title: Fictional project survey
nodes.body:
# Fictional project survey

This authored example surveys all four fixture source/spec/test files. It is not a transcript of an independent agent run. The fixture has no independent application revision: it is shipped inside the toolkit repository, whose Git commit identifies the exact version.

Created [[areas/pickups|pickup]] and [[areas/access|access]] maps, three behavior notes and three questions with different next actions. The accepted packed cancellation requirement diverges from code. Partner behavior is undecided. Deployment evidence is deliberately absent.

Executed `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from the fictional project: **PASS, 3 tests**. Reviewed source fingerprints were then accepted for the example; view generation does not make application claims true. Release checks, separate agent evaluations and browser observations are reported in the toolkit's `VALIDATION.md`.

See [[00-index|the index]] and [[01-coverage|coverage]]. No external system was queried and no real product behavior is implied.
